subject: Temporary staging headroom for 'EdgePilot' pilot - slice negotiation
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term staging headroom for EdgePilot pilot (2-week window)

Hi team,

Quick ask — EdgePilot (Zoe copied) wants to start a customer pilot next Monday. Product needs a modest temporary headroom in staging to run their live traffic spike testing (scale + latency profiling) for ~10 business days.

What we need from infra/ops: a temporary reserved slice (2x of their standard staging quota) from 7/6–7/17 with an autoscaling policy exception so the slice can burst above the usual cap for short periods. We want to avoid any preemption for the pilot window (they're running long-running latency-sensitive scenarios).

Attached: pilot_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx (SLA breakdown + expected token/sec profile) and a short capacity plan draft.

Questions:
- Is a short reservation feasible without impacting Q3 pilot capacity commitments?
- Any changes we need to policy-wise to allow burst > cap for a timeboxed window?
- Ops/infra owners who should own the MOP?

Kimberly/Karthik — can you review and flag major blockers? I can push a simple mutual action plan if we have the green light.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Dedicated 
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: pilot_sla_matrix_v1.xlsx]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term staging headroom for EdgePilot pilot (2-week window)

Laura — thanks for the heads up. A few notes from infra side after a quick skim:

1) Feasibility: We can carve a temporary slice, but we need to scope whether it must be dedicated GPUs (no sharing) or if a soft-reservation with preemption guards is acceptable. Dedicated GPUs reduce risk but takes a longer lead time to provision depending on current pool consumption.

2) Autoscale exception: We can allow a timeboxed policy override (start/end times) that lifts the hard burst cap to the requested level and re-applies the cap at window end. That requires ops approval and an explicit rollback plan in case other higher-priority traffic shows up.

3) Risk: If we mark the slice non-preemptible, we must tag it as "pilot-sla" and route lower-priority jobs elsewhere; this will require a short-term backfill plan for other teams.

Action items I propose:
- Confirm exact GPU count and whether NVLink/instance type is required (Laura/EdgePilot).
- Ops to sign-off on rollback and manual preemption override (Irene + Ops lead).
- Kimberly to confirm whether product can accept a soft-reservation vs hard carveout.

Irene — can you own the ops sign-off and coordination with on-call to ensure we have a rollback playbook? If we can get numbers by EOD today, I'll do a quick pollution check against the pool.

-Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Zoe Park <zoe@edgepilot.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term staging headroom for EdgePilot pilot (2-week window)

Thanks Karthik + Laura — copying Zoe so EdgePilot knows the cadence.

High-level response: ops can approve a timeboxed soft-reservation with an elevated burst cap and a 1-hour manual preemption SLA if capacity pressure occurs. I prefer soft-reservation for two reasons: faster to enact, and safer for juggling other commitments. We'll mark the reservation with pilot tag and an explicit rollback checklist.

I put together a short mutual action plan below (I'll own coordination):
- 2026-07-02 12:00 PDT: Laura to confirm requested GPU type and peak qps/token rate (reply to this thread).
- 2026-07-02 17:00 PDT: Karthik to run pool impact simulation and confirm feasibility (will include eviction risk).
- 2026-07-03 10:00 PDT: Ops (Irene) to provision soft-reservation in staging and set the elevated burst cap (start 07/06 00:00 PDT).
- 2026-07-06 00:00 PDT: Pilot window begins; on-call notified for 24/7 rolling watch for first 72 hours.
- 2026-07-17 23:59 PDT: Reservation auto-rolls back; ops to validate normal cap restored.

Rollbacks & Escalation: If preemption required, we will provide 60 minutes notice to pilot team (Zoe) and product; ops will attempt transverse-burst throttling before hard preemption.

Can Kimberly confirm product is fine with the 60-minute notice SLA and soft-reservation model?

Irene
Irene Choi
Operations Lead, Dedicated 
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: capacity_plan_v2.pdf]

On Wed, Jul 1, 2026 at 11:10 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Laura — thanks for the heads up. A few notes from infra side after a quick skim:
> ...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term staging headroom for EdgePilot pilot (2-week window)

Irene — the 60-minute notice SLA for hard preemption is OK from product side. A couple of clarifications:

- Laura: please confirm whether EdgePilot needs GPU type A100-80GB or can run on 40GB / q4-n quantized variant. The latter will make soft-reservation cheaper and reduce interference risk.
- If we go soft-reservation, we want an SLI guardrail: if 3rd-party latency/regression is detected (SLO breach), product agrees to throttle or pause the pilot on request.

If the pilot can accept the quantized variant and the SLI guardrail, product approves the plan.

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Zoe Park <zoe@edgepilot.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term staging headroom for EdgePilot pilot (2-week window)

Hi all — thanks for the prompt coordination. EdgePilot is comfortable with a quantized 40GB variant for most scenarios; we'll reserve single tests on 80GB for worst-case loads (estimate 4–6 hours total across the window). The 60-minute notice SLA is acceptable.

I'll send the final pilot runbook tonight and confirm exact peak qps numbers by EOD. Appreciate the flexibility — excited to get the pilot started.

—Zoe
Zoe Park
Head of Integrations, EdgePilot
zoe@edgepilot.ai
